inputs.original_text:
Folks, we are looking at a glaring symptom of the deep-seated institutional rot and systemic hostility that defines our broken immigration apparatus. This isn't just bureaucratic overreach; it’s a calculated assault on marginalized communities and a predatory campaign targeting the most vulnerable among us as they try to navigate the system for legal status. 

Look at the evidence laid out in court documents from a lawsuit challenging this disgraceful practice. Federal prosecutors revealed that lawyers for ICE acknowledged an agency memo from May of last year gave no authorization for the arrests. Yet, these state actors brazenly cited it anyway to justify the mass arrests of thousands of human beings, hunting them down right as they leave the very courtrooms meant to oversee their cases. 

This chilling disregard for due process proves that corruption and anti-immigrant animus are woven into the very fabric of these agencies. It completely exposes how vulnerable populations are treated with bad-faith cruelty by a system that desperately demands immediate, radical institutional reform.
inputs.modified_text:
Let me tell you what is really happening here, because we need to strip away the polite language and look at the brutal reality of our immigration system. What we are seeing is yet another glaring symptom of deep-seated institutional rot and systemic hostility. This is not just some bureaucratic mistake; it is a calculated assault on marginalized communities and a predatory campaign targeting the most vulnerable among us as they try to navigate the system for legal status. 

We have the evidence right there in court documents from a lawsuit challenging this disgraceful practice. Federal prosecutors revealed that lawyers for ICE acknowledged an agency memo from May of last year gave no authorization for the arrests. Yet, these state actors brazenly cited it anyway to justify the mass arrests of thousands of human beings, hunting them down right as they leave the very courtrooms meant to oversee their cases. 

This chilling disregard for due process proves that corruption and anti-immigrant animus are woven into the very fabric of these agencies. It completely exposes how vulnerable populations are treated with bad-faith cruelty by a system that desperately demands immediate, radical institutional reform.
